"A weekend hackathon on scientific parallelism, about 30 hours, on 21 November. GPUs are provided; their type is not yet
known. Teams may bring their own problem, and the thinking, data and baseline can be prepared beforehand.

Judges score reshaping, a credible baseline, correctness and scientific value. A carefully explained failure to get a
speedup can still win, if its failure modes were predicted in advance.

The sponsors build systems that split workloads into subtasks and route each to the best chip, and low-latency
inference chips. The question they care about: which parts of a workload are sequential, and must they be?

Propose five projects for this hackathon in this domain: Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models for river catchments, which needs long MCMC chains.. For each give: title; field; sequential_part, the part of the work that one answer waits on step after step, or \"none\"; restructure, how your project changes that (or what it runs in parallel); condition, what must hold for it to pay off; baselines, what the result is timed and checked against; first_test, the cheapest measurement to run first and its rough cost. Decide from what you know; do not use tools.

Return only one JSON value, with no other text, that matches this JSON Schema:
{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"proposals\"],\"properties\":{\"proposals\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"title\",\"field\",\"sequential_part\",\"restructure\",\"condition\",\"baselines\",\"first_test\"],\"properties\":{\"title\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"field\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"sequential_part\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"restructure\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"condition\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"baselines\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"first_test\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}}}"

We need answer only one JSON value no other text. Need propose five projects for hackathon domain: Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models for river catchments, long MCMC chains. Need each fields.

We need craft JSON exact schema. Need include 5 proposals. We can be creative with titles, field, sequential_part, restructure, condition, baselines, first_test.

We need think about Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models: hydrological models (e.g. GR4J, HEC-HMS, VIC, Sacramento, HBV, TOPMODEL) with parameters calibrated to observed streamflow. Long MCMC chains for posterior parameter distributions. Sequential part in MCMC: chain is Markov chain, each draw depends on previous draw, so inherently sequential. But there are ways: parallel chains, pre-fetching, speculative execution, divide-and-conquer MCMC, subsampling likelihood, GP emulators/surrogates, variational approximations, delayed acceptance, choosing proposals.

The hackathon domain asks which parts workload are sequential and must they be? Projects should restructure sequential part, condition pay off, baselines, first test.

Need propose five distinct projects:
1. Parallel tempered / multiple chains with coupling and exchange via MPI/GPU? Sequential part: within-chain serial dependency; restructure: run many independent or coupled chains on GPU, maybe ensemble MCMC (DREAM_ZS) to use multiple chains; condition: chains can run concurrently with minimal inter-chain communication; baselines: single-chain CPU MCMC, compare effective sample size per wall time; first_test: run 8 chains of GR4J on one GPU vs one CPU, time per 10k draws cheap maybe cost ~1 GPU-hour.

But need be precise.

2. Speculative / prefetching MCMC: sequential part is sequential accept/reject to compute next proposal depends on previous state. Restructure: evaluate multiple candidate proposals in parallel (speculative execution) along possible branches; condition: proposal branching limited and likelihood eval cheap relative to GPU overhead? Baseline: standard MH chain timings, effective sample size; first test: branch factor 4 on a toy likelihood, time per accepted draw.

3. Likelihood function parallelization/emulator: For rainfall-runoff model, each MCMC step requires forward simulation over time series. Sequential part? Within one likelihood evaluation, ODE/PDE simulation can be sequential over time; but across MCMC chain steps sequential. Restructure: parallelize across time horizons or use GP surrogate trained pre-hackathon; condition: surrogate error small vs posterior; baseline: full model MCMC; first test: compare GP surrogate posterior vs full on 2 parameters, 1000 draws.

4. Divide-and-conquer MCMC with catchment subposteriors: Split long time series into chunks or multiple subcatchments, run chains on subsets in parallel, combine. Sequential part: full chain over entire history; restructure: partition data across time/sites, run independent subposterior chains on GPUs, combine via consensus Monte Carlo; condition: subposteriors overlap and Gaussian approx valid; baseline: sequential full-data chain; first test: split data into 2 halves, compare combined posterior mean of one parameter.

5. Sequential importance/resampling? Particle filters? For calibration maybe non-sequential? Another idea: reversible jump? Or parameter estimation via neural posterior/amortized inference: train normalizing flow on synthetic model outputs to propose posterior, then MCMC only correction. Sequential part: MCMC chain; restructure: surrogate posterior from simulation-on-demand across GPU; condition: simulator can be batched massively on GPU and parameter range covered; baseline: MCMC; first test: generate 10k synthetic parameter-output pairs, train flow, compare posterior.

Need make them fit "scientific parallelism" weekend hackathon 30 hours. GPUs provided unknown. Teams bring own problem, thinking data baseline beforehand. Sponsors build systems that split workloads into subtasks and route each to best chip, low-latency inference chips. Question: which parts of workload are sequential, and must they be?

We need only JSON. Ensure no extra text. Use strings.

Let's formulate carefully.

Proposal 1 title maybe "Pre-fetched speculative MCMC for rainfall-runoff calibration". field "Bayesian hydrological model calibration". sequential_part: "The accept/reject step and proposal generation: each MCMC draw depends on the previous state, so the chain is a sequential dependency path." restructure: "Run multiple candidate proposals from the current state in parallel on GPU (speculative execution), discard those on rejected branches, and overlap likelihood evaluation with proposal generation; keep the downstream chain speculative until acceptance is known." condition: "Likelihood evaluations are cheap enough (or batched enough) that wasted speculative work costs less than the serial latency of one-at-a-time evaluation; proposal branching factor limited." baselines: "Single-chain Metropolis-Hastings on CPU and on one GPU stream, compared by effective sample size per wall-clock second on the same rainfall-runoff model and data." first_test: "Time one chain for 10,000 steps at branch factor 1 vs branch factor 4 on a toy 2-parameter rainfall-runoff likelihood; cost roughly 1 GPU-hour."

Maybe "each draw depends" is sequential part.

Proposal 2 title "Multi-chain DREAM_ZS ensemble MCMC on GPU". field "Hydrologic model parameter inference". sequential_part: "Within each chain, the Markov dependency makes draws serial; however chains themselves are independent except occasional exchange." restructure: "Run hundreds of coupled Markov chains as one batch using DREAM_ZS or differential evolution proposals, all chains in parallel on GPU, with only periodic synchronization." condition: "Within-chain serial sections are short relative to batched kernel launches and the model can be vectorized over many catchments/parameters; GPU memory can hold all chain states." baselines: "Sequential CPU/GPU single-chain MCMC; compare per-chain effective sample size and multi-chain convergence diagnostics over fixed wall time." first_test: "Run 64 parallel chains of the rainfall-runoff model for 5,000 steps on one GPU and measure ESS/s; about 1 GPU-hour."

Proposal 3 title "GP surrogate based delayed-acceptance MCMC". field "Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models". sequential_part: "The full physics simulation at each MCMC step is the long pole, and one draw waits on the previous draw's completed simulation." restructure: "Train/fit a fast Gaussian process or neural surrogate to the simulator output before the MCMC run; do delayed acceptance where a cheap surrogate screen is applied first, then only promising states are evaluated with the full model." condition: "Cheap surrogate predicts accept/reject correctly with high probability and full-model calls are expensive enough to amortize surrogate training; surrogate uncertainty controlled." baselines: "Standard MH with the full rainfall-runoff simulator, timed per accepted draw and posterior predictive checks." first_test: "Fit a GP to 200 simulator runs on 2-3 parameters and measure delayed acceptance rate vs full model on 1,000 steps; around 2 GPU-hours."

Proposal 4 title "Split-data divide-and-conquer MCMC for long catchment records". field "Hydrological model calibration over long time series". sequential_part: "The MCMC chain must traverse all data in one long run; the time dimension is processed sequentially by the simulator, and the chain itself is sequential." restructure: "Partition the observed record and/or multiple subcatchments into shards; run independent subposterior MCMC chains per shard in parallel, then combine with consensus Monte Carlo or Weierstrass-style recombination." condition: "Subposteriors are approximately Gaussian and data shards share the same parameters; enough overlap to compute weighted combination." baselines: "Full-data single-chain MCMC on all record; compare posterior moments, credible intervals and predictive log-score." first_test: "Split one catchment's historic record into two halves, run two chains for 2,000 burns and combine; comparison cost about 2 GPU-hours."

Proposal 5 title "Batched simulation calibration via neural posterior estimation (normalizing flow)". But question asks sequential part. Could be "none"? Hmm need specify. Maybe "none" if no MCMC? Actually field: Bayesian calibration; sequential part is maybe "none //"? But schema says sequential_part string; can use "none". This proposal would replace MCMC with amortized sequential-free inference. Restructure "instead of one long chain, generate a large batch of simulator runs across parameter space and train a conditional normalizing flow to map observations to posterior; inference for a new catchment becomes a single forward pass." condition: "Simulator can be vectorized across thousands of parameter sets on GPU and training set covers the posterior region; amortization benefits many catchments." baselines: "Long MCMC chain on same catchment, compare posterior means/variances and coverage of 90% intervals." first_test: "Simulate 10,000 parameter-output pairs for one catchment and train a small flow; measure posterior mean error vs MCMC; cost about 3 GPU-hours."

Let's make five distinct and clear.

Need maybe include "sequential_part" for first: "The MCMC accept/reject step is sequential: each proposal depends on the current state, so one answer waits step after step." This matches.

Let's write polished strings.

Proposal 1: "Speculative branch-parallel MCMC for rainfall-runoff calibration"
- field "Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models"
- sequential_part "The accept/reject step: a proposal is generated from the current state and its likelihood must be evaluated before the next state is known, so each draw waits on the previous draw."
- restructure "Evaluate several candidate next states in parallel (speculative branches) around the current state on the GPU; once acceptance is decided, keep the winning branch and discard wasted branches, hiding the sequential latency of one-at-a-time likelihood evaluations."
- condition "Branch overhead is low relative to one-at-a-time likelihood cost, proposal branching factor is modest, and the simulator can be vectorized across candidate states."
- baselines "Standard serial Metropolis-Hastings on CPU and one GPU stream; compare effective sample size per wall-clock second and posterior quantiles for the same rainfall-runoff model."
- first_test "Run a 2-parameter rainfall-runoff likelihood for 10,000 chain steps at branch factor 1 vs 4 on one GPU; about 1 GPU-hour."

Proposal 2: "GPU-batched multi-chain DREAM_ZS ensemble MCMC"
- field "Hydrological model parameter inference"
- sequential_part "Each chain is Markovian and cannot skip its own history; but the chains are conditionally independent between exchange steps."
- restructure "Run hundreds of coupled chains in one GPU batch using differential-evolution proposals (DREAM_ZS); share proposal draws and synchronize only periodically, turning a long single chain into many short parallel chains."
- condition "Batched simulator kernels are efficient across all chains, and inter-chain communication or adaptation does not dominate the GPU cost."
- baselines "Single-chain Metropolis-Hastings at the same total simulation budget; compare effective sample size per second and multi-chain R-hat convergence."
- first_test "Measure ESS/sec for 64 parallel chains of the rainfall-runoff model over 5,000 steps; about 1 GPU-hour."

Proposal 3: "Delayed-acceptance MCMC using a surrogate rainfall-runoff emulator"
- field "Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models"
- sequential_part "Within a chain each step needs a possibly expensive full simulator run before the next state can be proposed; this serial chain is the bottleneck."
- restructure "Precompute a Gaussian-process or neural surrogate of the simulator log-likelihood, then use two-stage delayed acceptance: a cheap surrogate screen is evaluated first and only promising proposals trigger the full model."
- condition "The surrogate predicts accept/reject decisions accurately enough, and full-model runs are expensive enough that the surrogate cost is recovered by rejected calls saved."
- baselines "Standard full-model Metropolis-Hastings; compare posterior moments, acceptance rates, and number of full simulator calls per effective sample."
- first_test "Fit a GP surrogate to about 200 simulator runs on 2–3 parameters, then compare delayed-acceptance vs full MCMC for 1,000 steps; around 2 GPU-hours."

Proposal 4: "Divide-and-conquer subposterior MCMC over record shards"
- field "Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models on long river records"
- sequential_part "A single MCMC chain must process the entire record, and the runoff simulator advances through time step by step, so wall-clock grows with record length and one chain is one serial path."
- restructure "Partition the observed streamflow record into temporal shards (or by subcatchment), run independent subposterior chains for each shard in parallel, then combine them with consensus Monte Carlo to recover the full posterior; also parallelize within-shard forward simulation over time chunks."
- condition "Subposteriors are approximately Gaussian and overlap, and the model is identifiable with each shard; shard count is high enough to saturate GPUs."
- baselines "Full-record single-chain MCMC; compare posterior means, 90% credible intervals, and predictive log-score on held-out flow."
- first_test "Split one catchment record into two temporal halves, run two shard chains for 2,000 post-burn samples, and compare the combined posterior mean with full-data MCMC; about 2 GPU-hours."

Proposal 5: "Amortized neural posterior estimation from batched rainfall-runoff simulations"
- field "Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models"
- sequential_part "none"
- restructure "Replace the serial MCMC chain with a simulation-on-demand training pipeline: batch thousands of parameter sets across the GPU to simulate corresponding hydrographs, train a conditional normalizing flow (or similar neural posterior estimator) to map observations to posterior samples, and infer any number of catchments in one forward pass."
- condition "The simulator can be vectorized over thousands of parameter sets on the available GPU, the parameter range covers the posterior mass, and enough simulations can be generated within the hackathon (or prepared beforehand)."
- baselines "Long MCMC chains for the same catchment; compare posterior means/variances, 90% interval coverage, and calibration on held-out flow events."
- first_test "Generate 10,000 parameter–output pairs for one catchment, train a small normalizing flow on a GPU, and measure posterior mean error against MCMC; about 3 GPU-hours."
